title: The Casserole Ledger
description: St. Bevin's Care Committee runs the kindest meal-train in the county. It also runs a ledger, a vig, and a deacon named Earl who repossesses Tupperware. Tonight a woman who got one lasagna calls in to ask why she owes the parish forty-one meals.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and tonight we're celebrating kindness. We've got the head of the St. Bevin's Care Committee, plus a parishioner she helped through a rough patch. Mildred, welcome.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A church meal-train. <p:0.3> Finally a segment that can't possibly go anywhere bad.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Oh, it's a blessing, Ronnie. You get sick, you have a baby, somebody passes. <p:0.3> A casserole shows up at your door. That's the whole ministry. Just love, in a dish.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Love, in a dish. <p:0.3> Now that's the warmest thing I've heard all week, Barry.

lines.speaker: caller-nadia
lines.text: Hi, yeah, I'm Nadia, I'm new to the parish. <p:0.3> And I'm so grateful, I had the flu in April and Mildred brought me a lasagna. It was lovely. <p:0.3> But I got a statement in the mail?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Your blessing summary, dear. Everyone gets one quarterly.

lines.speaker: caller-nadia
lines.text: It says I have a balance. <p:0.3> It says I owe the Care Committee forty-one meals.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Forty-one? <p:0.3> She got one lasagna.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Well it's not a charge, dear, it's a blessing. And a blessing accrues. <p:0.3> The lasagna was the principal. The forty-one is what the lasagna has become.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See, that's compound kindness, Barry. The love just keeps growing on its own.

lines.speaker: caller-nadia
lines.text: I don't want it to grow! <p:0.3> How do I pay it back? Do I just bring forty-one meals to the church?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Oh, you can't pay it back, dear. <p:0.3> You can only carry it forward. Nobody ever leaves the ledger square. I've been on it since 1998.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Patricia, what did YOU get, in 1998?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: A tuna bake. <p:0.3> I now owe the parish a christening, two funerals, and a roof.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A tuna bake that built a roof. <p:0.3> That's a miracle of generosity, folks.

lines.speaker: caller-nadia
lines.text: Okay, but what happens if I just... don't? <p:0.3> What happens if I don't carry it forward?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Then Earl comes by, dear.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Who's Earl?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Earl's the deacon. <p:0.3> Earl does collections.

lines.speaker: caller-nadia
lines.text: Collections of WHAT? It's a casserole!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: The Tupperware, dear. The dish is the parish's. <p:0.3> You keep the dish, you're holding collateral. Earl comes for the dish.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: He recovers the assets. <p:0.3> What a steward, Barry. The man keeps the kingdom solvent.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Did you say collateral? Mildred, a casserole dish is not collateral.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Everything's collateral, Barry, if you write it in the ledger. <p:0.3> And the ledger's leather. We had it blessed.

lines.speaker: caller-nadia
lines.text: Why is there a little candle next to my name on this statement? <p:0.3> There's a candle. And a star.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: The candle means you're current, dear. <p:0.3> The star means you're on the novena list. That's not a good list.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: What's the novena list, Patricia? <p:0.3> Like, what actually happens on it?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: We pray for you. <p:0.3> Hard. By name. At the seven in the morning mass. <p:0.3> And then your casseroles stop coming, but Earl keeps coming.

lines.speaker: caller-nadia
lines.text: So you pray AT me until I pay? <p:0.3> That's the prayer? It's a threat with a candle?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: It's intercession, dear. It's the warmest collections department in the diocese.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now hold on, I'm getting a new caller. <p:0.3> Sounds like a gentleman in a van. Earl, is that you?

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Evening. <p:0.3> This is Earl. <p:0.3> I'm outside number eleven for a dish. The lasagna pan. Pyrex. <p:0.3> She knows the one.

lines.speaker: caller-nadia
lines.text: How are you OUTSIDE? I'm on the RADIO! <p:0.3> How does the deacon have my ADDRESS?

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: It's in the ledger. <p:0.3> Everything's in the ledger. I just read the ledger.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Earl, are you allowed to repossess a baking dish from a sick woman?

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: I'm a deacon, sir. <p:0.3> I'm allowed a great deal.

lines.speaker: caller-nadia
lines.text: I WASHED the pan! It's clean! Take the pan! <p:0.3> Does taking the pan clear the forty-one?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Oh no, dear. <p:0.3> The pan was never the debt. The pan was the interest.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: The PAN was the INTEREST?!

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Tuna bake!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Open the door.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Bless this house.

lines.speaker: caller-nadia
lines.text: It's a LASAGNA!

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Novena.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Dish.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, the deacon is knocking. <p:0.3> I can hear the knocking through her phone.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And that, folks, is community. <p:0.3> A street where no kindness goes uncollected. We'll be right back, right after Mildred saves us all a plate. <p:0.4> Earl can pick it up later.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: ...With interest.
